idiom_name: map[[2]int][]*Entity hash grid (or [][]*Entity for bounded worlds)
implementation_notes: Go has no spatial container in the standard library; the manual realization is a map keyed by a cell coordinate ([2]int or a custom struct) whose values are []*Entity slices, or a flat [][]*Entity grid for a bounded world. Map iteration order is unspecified and maps are not safe for concurrent writes, so a grid shared between goroutines needs a mutex or per-goroutine partitions. The hand grid stays idiomatic and allocation-light for gameplay; third-party quadtree packages exist (for example pkg.go.dev/github.com/s0rg/quadtree) but none is standard.
pitfalls: Concurrent map writes panic; an entity grid touched by several goroutines must be guarded or partitioned per goroutine.
Slices stored in the map share backing arrays after append, so copying a cell slice and appending can mutate the grid; copy when returning.
Keying by float coordinates directly invites rounding drift; always key by integer cell coordinates.
